rules.description: Redacts the value assigned to a key whose final segment names a secret, such as password=, DB_PASSWORD=, "clientSecret": or --password. Keys are split into segments at _, -, . and camel-case transitions.
limitations: Unquoted values end at whitespace, , ; & quotes and brackets, so an unquoted password containing those characters is only partly redacted; quoted values are fully handled.
Multi-line strings, arrays, and objects are not treated as assigned values.
rules.name: Named secret values

rules.description: Redacts the credential in Authorization and Proxy-Authorization fields while keeping a recognized scheme name. Parameterized schemes such as Digest are redacted to the end of the field; when the first word is not a recognized scheme, the whole field is redacted.
limitations: Credentials are never decoded; header names other than the two listed are not covered.
An unrecognized scheme name is redacted together with its credential.
rules.name: Authorization credentials

rules.description: Redacts the password in scheme://user:password@host for any scheme, keeping scheme, user, host, port, path, query, and fragment.
limitations: User information without a password separator is not covered; reserved delimiters inside passwords must be percent-encoded.
rules.name: URL credentials

rules.description: Redacts the username segment of /home/<user>, /Users/<user>, and C:\Users\<user> paths, including JSON-escaped Windows separators, keeping the rest of the path.
limitations: UNC paths, ~user, C:\Documents and Settings\, and personal names elsewhere in text are not covered.
rules.name: Home-directory usernames

rules.description: Redacts email-shaped strings using a pragmatic ASCII grammar. Inside a URL authority, only the username part can match.
limitations: Quoted local parts, internationalized addresses, address literals, and single-label domains are not covered.
rules.name: Email addresses

rules.description: Redacts RFC 1918 IPv4 addresses and IPv6 unique-local addresses, keeping ports, CIDR suffixes, zone identifiers, and URL brackets.
limitations: Public, loopback, link-local, shared-address-space, and integer or hexadecimal IP encodings are not covered.
rules.name: Private IP addresses

rules.description: Redacts tokens with a documented, prefix-identifiable format wherever they appear. A run longer than the minimum is redacted whole.
limitations: Only the formats listed are recognized; high-entropy strings without a known prefix need a named key.
rules.name: Known credential formats

rules.description: Redacts the body of PEM and OpenSSH private-key blocks, multi-line or escaped on one line, keeping the armor lines and the line count.

examples.output: "pem": "-----BEGIN PRIVATE KEY-----[PRIVATE KEY REDACTED]-----END PRIVATE KEY-----"

limitations: An unterminated block is redacted to the end of the input and reported with a warning.
PuTTY .ppk files and binary or base64-wrapped key containers are not covered.
rules.name: Private-key blocks

rules.description: Redacts cookie values in Cookie and Set-Cookie fields, keeping cookie names and Set-Cookie attributes.
limitations: Cookies passed in other fields are covered only when their key names a secret (SR-001).
rules.name: Cookie values
